bodyParagraphs: Original heading/title: — The witness from the woman's household
QB-0251 — The witness from the woman's household Genesis No witness.
Qur'an A shāhid min ahlihā — “witness from her family/household” — proposes an evidentiary test.
Classification MAJOR QUR'ANIC NARRATIVE ADDITION relative to Genesis.
But given what we have repeatedly found in Surah 12, we should not yet classify the witness as uniquely Qur'anic.
We need to search pre-Islamic Jewish and Christian Joseph traditions.
What does “witness” mean? The Qur'an does not name this person.
man or woman, adult or child, whether the witness saw the struggle, whether the witness is related by blood, or whether the witness is merely a household member.
Later Islamic tradition supplies much more—including the famous story that the witness was an infant who miraculously spoke.
Qur'an 12:26 does not say the witness was a baby.
This is reminiscent of our cradle-Jesus work: later miraculous identification must not silently become Qur'anic wording.
QB-0251                 Qur'an introduces anonymous witness from woman's               Major addition; source-history OPEN household; Genesis has none
Pre-Islamic evidence Third-party witness: not securely demonstrated.
Front/back garment test: not securely demonstrated.
Classification GENESIS PARALLEL: none for the forensic mechanism.
PRE-ISLAMIC JEWISH PARALLEL: NOT CURRENTLY DEMONSTRATED.
PRE-ISLAMIC CHRISTIAN PARALLEL: NOT CURRENTLY DEMONSTRATED.
LOST ORAL/TRADITIONAL SOURCE: possible but unevidenced.
QUR'ANIC NARRATIVE DEVELOPMENT: possible and currently the safest positive literary description.
B. Did Potiphar know Joseph was innocent? Here the evidence is much more interesting.
Genesis 39:19–20 After hearing his wife's accusation:
But Genesis does not explicitly say:
Nor does it explicitly identify at whom Potiphar was angry.
That opened the door for interpretation.
5. Josephus gives the straightforward reading Josephus essentially follows the accusation → punishment trajectory.
Potiphar accepts the accusation sufficiently to punish Joseph.
That does not provide the Qur'anic parallel.
Josephus: negative for Potiphar recognizing Joseph's innocence.
6. But Jewish interpretation noticed a problem The problem is understandable.
Potiphar had already experienced Joseph as:
responsible for virtually the entire household.
Then suddenly his wife accuses this same servant of attempted sexual wrongdoing.
Interpreters therefore asked whether Potiphar really believed her.
This becomes especially significant in rabbinic interpretation.

7. Genesis Rabbah provides the important pre-Islamic trajectory Genesis Rabbah's treatment of the Joseph/Potiphar episode contains traditions protecting Joseph's innocence and complicating the straightforward idea that Potiphar simply accepted his wife's story.
This is securely relevant because Genesis Rabbah belongs broadly to fifth-century Palestinian Judaism, well before Islam.
The tradition knows that Joseph is righteous and that the woman's accusation is false.
But we need to phrase the Potiphar conclusion precisely:
Pre-Islamic rabbinic interpretation already problematized a simple “Potiphar believed his wife because the garment proved Joseph guilty” reading.
What is not secure is claiming Genesis Rabbah contains the Qur'an's exact:
husband sees rear tear → announces wife's scheme → tells her to seek forgiveness.
8. A particularly interesting Jewish solution: Potiphar's punishment was restrained A strand of Jewish interpretation reasons from the relatively limited punishment itself.
If Potiphar truly believed Joseph had attempted to rape his wife, Joseph—as a slave—might have faced death.
That can be interpreted as evidence that Potiphar was not fully convinced of Joseph's guilt.
This does not equal the Qur'an's explicit exoneration, but it moves toward:
Potiphar knew or suspected there was more to the story.
That's a meaningful pre-Islamic interpretive trajectory.
9. And the Testament of Joseph gives us another interesting angle
The Testament of Joseph portrays Potiphar's wife as repeatedly manipulating circumstances and making false claims about Joseph.
Joseph's innocence is absolutely clear to the audience.
But again, we don't get the Qur'anic judicial scene in which her husband evaluates the physical evidence and explicitly concludes:
Potiphar explicitly recognizing it: traditions move in that direction.
QB-0251 — Witness / front-back shirt test Exact pre-Islamic parallel: ❌ NOT DEMONSTRATED
QB-0251 — CORRECTED Third-party anonymous witness: exact pre-Islamic parallel not securely demonstrated.
Exact front/back tear test: exact correspondence still needs caution.
Garment used inferentially to establish Joseph's innocence: ✅ PRE-ISLAMIC CHRISTIAN PARALLEL CONFIRMED.
This is an important correction to preserve in the audit trail.
7. Now the biggest finding: Potiphar's wife eventually confesses This is where the Syriac tradition becomes remarkably relevant to Q12:51.
A pre-Islamic Syriac Joseph tradition associated with Pseudo-Narsai continues the story beyond Joseph's rise to power.
After Joseph becomes ruler, Potiphar becomes frightened.
Potiphar returns home and tells his wife.
Potiphar's wife admits that she was the one who attempted to seduce Joseph.
She subsequently becomes afraid, has a scribe compose a petition to Joseph, admits wrongdoing, asks forgiveness, and eventually appears before Joseph seeking mercy.
Joseph forgives her and sends her away in peace.                BYU Studies +1
That is a genuine extrabiblical parallel to the Qur'an's reappearance of Potiphar's wife.
This matters enormously because Genesis simply drops her Genesis:
→ she disappears permanently from the story.
But two expanded traditions refuse to let her disappear.
Syriac Christian Joseph tradition Joseph rises to power
“Indeed, he is one of the truthful.”
That is now a very significant parallel.
There is even a linguistic curiosity The Pseudo-Narsai tradition reportedly calls Joseph with Syriac terms from the root:
The Qur'an's wife says Joseph is:
These are cognate Semitic roots, though not the same word or necessarily the same semantic function.
That is interesting, but we must not overclaim it as evidence of direct borrowing.        Digital Collectio…
LINGUISTIC/CONCEPTUAL AFFINITY — not proof of dependence.
8. But there is a crucial chronological/order difference The Syriac tradition does not simply equal the Qur'an.
So the Qur'an moves the confession earlier.
It takes an existing extrabiblical motif—
—and makes it a prerequisite for Joseph's release and elevation.
That looks like literary restructuring rather than simple reproduction.
9. Joseph refusing release remains the distinctive component After checking these traditions, I do not find a securely pre-Islamic Jewish or Christian text containing the precise Q12:50 action:
No—first investigate the women and clear my reputation.
The Syriac confession traditions generally place the wife's confession after Joseph's elevation, rather than making it a condition for his departure from prison.
So at our current evidence level:

QB-0251: We previously said no pre-Islamic garment-based innocence test was securely demonstrated. Correction: pre-Islamic Syriac Christian material does use Joseph's garment as evidence relevant to his innocence; the exact Qur'anic front/back test remains less certain.                 First Things

bodyParagraphs: Original heading/title: — Why Joseph is imprisoned
QB-0252 — Why Joseph is imprisoned Genesis: follows wife's accusation and master's anger.
Qur'an: Joseph is vindicated before imprisonment.
Therefore imprisonment cannot straightforwardly result from the husband believing Joseph guilty.
This could become significant for the Qur'an's portrayal of injustice.
Surah 12:29 — “Joseph, turn away from this” The husband says:
This is another major difference from Genesis.
Tells Joseph to let matter drop.
QB-0252                 Genesis imprisonment follows accusation; Qur'an                OPEN through 12:35 vindicates Joseph before imprisonment
We can now substantially resolve the imprisonment issue.
The natural narrative connection is accusation → punishment.
she publicly admits Joseph resisted her.
she threatens Joseph with imprisonment unless he submits sexually.
Joseph says prison is preferable to sexual wrongdoing.
Qur'anic Joseph's imprisonment is not based on a successful false conviction.
It becomes the consequence of power, coercion and suppression despite known innocence.
We should keep QB-0252 open until 12:35, because that verse tells us the authorities' final decision.
But the divergence from Genesis is now unmistakable.
QB-0252                 Qur'anic imprisonment increasingly appears as                 Strongly strengthened; close at 12:35 punishment despite known innocence rather than mistaken conviction
And we should investigate QB-0254 before 12:35, because it is exactly the sort of episode where our methodology has repeatedly paid off:
Do the women, banquet, knives, and cut hands occur in any securely pre-Islamic Jewish or Christian Joseph tradition?

We should break that into components—women gathering to see Joseph; Potiphar's wife deliberately displaying Joseph to justify her desire; knives/fruit; women accidentally cutting themselves; and Joseph being described as superhuman/angelic—because an older source may preserve only part of the Qur'anic scene.
Do the women, banquet, knives, and cut hands occur in any securely pre-Islamic Jewish or Christian Joseph tradition?

Worked for 8s Yes. This one is much stronger than the bucket episode. There is evidence for a pre-Islamic Jewish version of essentially the same women/knives/cut-hands episode, although we need to be precise about which textual witness establishes the chronology.

QB-0252 — CLOSED: Why Joseph is imprisoned Genesis 39: the wife accuses Joseph → Potiphar becomes angry → Joseph is imprisoned. Genesis does not explicitly say “Potiphar believed her,” but narratively the imprisonment immediately follows her accusation.           Sefaria
Qur'an: the sequence is radically different:

woman accuses Joseph → shirt evidence exposes her → husband recognizes the deception → woman publicly admits Joseph resisted → she threatens imprisonment → Joseph prefers prison to sexual submission → authorities see the signs/evidence and nevertheless imprison him.                                       Quran
So the Qur'an has transformed Joseph's imprisonment into:
punishment despite known evidence of innocence.
That's stronger than what we could establish at 12:32.
QB-0252                 Qur'an imprisons Joseph after evidence of innocence           CLOSED — major restructuring is known, unlike Genesis's accusation→imprisonment sequence

records.title: Potiphar/the Egyptian husband's response
bodyParagraphs: Original heading/title: — Potiphar/the Egyptian husband's response
QB-0253 — Potiphar/the Egyptian husband's response Genesis 39:19–20 Master hears wife's accusation.
Qur'an 12:28–29 Husband recognizes wife's deception and Joseph's innocence.
He asks Joseph not to pursue/publicize the matter and tells wife to seek forgiveness.
This should become especially important when we investigate pre-Islamic retellings:
Did Jewish or Christian interpreters ever portray Potiphar as knowing Joseph was innocent?
If yes, the Qur'an may align with an extrabiblical tradition.
If no, this is a significant Qur'anic restructuring.
There is also an intriguing theological difference The husband says:
But the Qur'an doesn't explicitly tell us:
In Qur'anic usage, istighfār overwhelmingly concerns seeking forgiveness from God.
Yet here the speaker is an Egyptian character.
That raises questions we shouldn't overread:
Does the Qur'an portray this Egyptian household as believing in God? Is this simply the narrator's Arabic religious vocabulary? Does istaghfirī here mean more generally “ask forgiveness”?
Keep it lexical/theological rather than assuming an entire Egyptian theology from one imperative.
QB-0253                 Genesis master imprisons Joseph after accusation;              Major narrative difference; source- Qur'anic husband recognizes wife's guilt                       history OPEN
QB-0253 — REFINED We should therefore avoid either extreme.
It would be wrong to say:
“Before the Qur'an everyone simply understood Potiphar as believing his wife.”
But it would also be wrong to say:
“Genesis Rabbah already contains the Qur'an's exoneration scene.”
Pre-Islamic Jewish interpretation Joseph's innocence becomes heavily emphasized, and interpretation develops around the ambiguity of Potiphar's response and the unexpectedly limited punishment.
This creates a trajectory in which Potiphar may suspect or know that Joseph isn't guilty as charged.
PRE-ISLAMIC EXACT QUR'ANIC EXONERATION SCENE: NOT DEMONSTRATED.
QUR'ANIC DEVELOPMENT OF EXISTING INTERPRETIVE PROBLEM: plausible.
C. This gives us a very interesting developmental trajectory Put the sources in order:
Genesis Garment appears to support woman's accusation.
Potiphar's actual belief isn't explicitly described.
Pre-Islamic Jewish/Christian interpretation Joseph's innocence becomes increasingly emphasized.
His temptation becomes an enormous moral narrative.
Interpreters grapple with how such a righteous Joseph nevertheless ends up imprisoned.
And the very object that incriminates Joseph in Genesis—
—is transformed into the object that proves his innocence.
That is the key literary development.
Open this as a cumulative literary record:
QB-0253 — Potiphar knows/suspects Joseph's innocence Pre-Islamic interpretive trajectory: ✅ SUPPORTED
QB-0253 — UPGRADED AGAIN Our earlier classification was too cautious.
PRE-ISLAMIC POTIPHAR KNOWS JOSEPH IS INNOCENT: ✅ CONFIRMED.
Genesis Rabbah preserves an explicit tradition in which Potiphar knows Joseph is innocent.
That significantly changes our source-history reconstruction.
5. Syriac Christianity gets even closer Pre-Islamic Syriac Joseph traditions also developed this same problem.
Recent comparative scholarship summarizes the witnesses this way:
Jubilees, Philo, Josephus, Ephrem, Pseudo-Ephrem and Jacob of Serugh generally retain the biblical trajectory in which Potiphar believes the accusation.
Genesis Rabbah, Pseudo-Basil, Pseudo-Narsai and Narsai
contain versions in which Potiphar does not believe his wife's accusation, although he nevertheless imprisons Joseph.            Digital Collectio… +1
Potiphar recognizing Joseph's innocence was circulating in both Jewish and Christian interpretive environments before Islam.
This is no longer merely a rabbinic curiosity.
6. And the garment evidence itself has a pre-Islamic Christian antecedent This requires a correction to something we said earlier.
Earlier we classified the Qur'an's shirt-based exoneration as lacking a securely demonstrated pre-Islamic parallel.

The stronger scholarly evidence now shows that Syriac Christian homilies attributed to Narsai/Pseudo- Narsai contain garment reasoning connected with Joseph's innocence. Modern scholarship specifically notes these fifth-century Syriac parallels.                First Things +1
That does not necessarily mean the exact Qur'anic front-versus-back tear test appears identically.
garment → rational evidence of Joseph's innocence
So we need to revise QB-0251 accordingly.

QB-0253: We previously classified a pre-Islamic Potiphar-doubts trajectory merely as “supported.” Upgrade: Genesis Rabbah and Syriac witnesses establish a pre-Islamic tradition in which Potiphar knows/recognizes Joseph's innocence yet imprisons him anyway.                             Scribd +1

This turns Q12:25–51 into one of the strongest examples so far of the Qur'an participating in a Late Antique interpretive development of Genesis: several elements absent from Genesis—Potiphar knowing Joseph is innocent, evidentiary use of the garment, and the wife's eventual confession—already existed before Islam. What remains especially Qur'an-specific is their reorganization into a formal vindication sequence before Joseph accepts freedom and political elevation.
Surah 12:58 — Joseph's brothers arrive in Egypt ‫َو َج اَء ِإْخ َو ُة ُي وُس َف َف َد َخ ُلوا َع َل ْيِه َف َع َرَف ُه ْم َو ُه ْم َل ُه ُم نِك ُروَن‬
“Joseph's brothers came and entered before him. He recognized them, while they did not recognize him.”

This is an extremely close parallel to Genesis 42. The famine reaches Canaan; Jacob sends ten sons to Egypt but keeps Benjamin home. Joseph is governing Egypt's grain distribution. When the brothers appear, Joseph recognizes them and they fail to recognize him.                               Bible Gateway +1

Qur'an 12:30–31 All of those elements appear.
Do not classify it as a Qur'anic invention yet.
Joseph's extraordinary physical beauty was already a major theme in pre-Islamic Jewish Joseph interpretation.
the exact banquet + knives + cut-hands story.

beautiful in form and beautiful in appearance.

attempts seduction, promises wealth, threatens Joseph, manipulates him, and becomes consumed by desire.

QB-0254 — Investigation result: PRE-ISLAMIC PARALLEL CONFIRMED The familiar version occurs in Midrash Tanhuma, Vayeshev 5:2. Potiphar's wife gathers Egyptian women, gives each an etrog (citron) and a knife, brings Joseph before them, and while staring at his beauty they cut their hands. She then argues, in effect: if seeing him once does this to you, imagine seeing him continually.           Sefaria
That is remarkably close to Q12:30–32.

But Tanhuma itself cannot establish pre-Islamic priority. Its textual history is complicated, and scholarship commonly places its edited form in the early medieval period; older traditions are embedded within it.         My Jewish Learn…
The important evidence lies behind Tanhuma.

The Palestinian Aramaic poetic witness Meir Bar-Ilan's 2016 study draws upon Jewish Palestinian Aramaic poetry published by Michael Sokoloff and Joseph Yahalom. The relevant alphabetical Aramaic poem contains the same narrative:
→ invites female friends to a feast
→ they stare at his extraordinary beauty

Bar-Ilan dates this poetic material to the Byzantine period, approximately the fourth–sixth centuries CE, based in part on its linguistic environment and Greek vocabulary, and therefore regards it as pre- Qur'anic.          ResearchGate

More generally, specialists place Palestinian Jewish Aramaic liturgical poetry in Late Antiquity; modern collections contain Palestinian Aramaic poems from approximately the fourth through seventh centuries.          Religious Studies

So unlike our bucket investigation, we have a credible Late Antique Jewish witness anchoring this narrative before or around the threshold of Islam, with scholarship specifically arguing for a fourth– sixth-century date for this Joseph material.                    ResearchGate

Joseph deliberately displayed before them                       Yes                            Yes
Each woman receives a knife                                     Yes                            Yes

That is an exceptionally close narrative correspondence.                       Sefaria +1
There is an even older layer behind it The complete knife scene isn't the beginning of the tradition.

The Jewish Greek work Joseph and Aseneth, usually dated somewhere around the late Second Temple/Roman period, already portrays Joseph as so extraordinarily beautiful that Egyptian wives and daughters desire him intensely when they see him. Joseph repeatedly rejects their approaches because he will not sin against the God of Israel.                The Torah
So we can see a developmental trajectory:
Joseph's beauty affects many Egyptian women, not merely Potiphar's wife.
→ her own attraction is thereby vindicated.
“That is the one concerning whom you blamed me.”
The continuity is substantial.             The Torah +1
But the Qur'an does something interesting with the fruit The Jewish version explains why they have knives:
“She gave each one of them a knife.”
This means later Muslim commentators who supply fruit are filling an apparent narrative gap—and that detail has a striking Jewish analogue.
But we should not insert the fruit into the Qur'anic text.

worth investigating; it does not by itself identify the transmission route or prove direct literary copying.           ResearchGate

packets.title: Comparison Joseph Dream Dead Mother
paragraphs: Comparison — Dead mother in Joseph’s dream
Genesis 37:10 / Genesis Rabbah 84:11 beside Quran 12:4, 12:100 and early tafsīr.
Date: 29 September 2026. DRAFT / UNPUBLISHED. QB-0336 / QDISC-0641. Not a merge.
1. The Jewish problem (pre-Islamic)

Genesis 37:10. Jacob glosses the dream: shall I and your mother and your brothers come and bow? Rachel is already dead in the Genesis order (35:16–19). Joseph already has eleven brothers, so Benjamin exists.
Genesis Rabbah 84:11. R. Levi in the name of R. Hama b. Hanina: that I and your brothers is one thing; what about I and your mother? Rachel is dead, and you say I and your mother.
Solutions already listed there and in the Talmud: the moon is Bilhah who raised him as a mother; or every dream has worthless bits (Berakhot 55), so the mother-piece need not happen.
2. What the Quran names
12:4. Eleven stars, the sun, and the moon prostrating. No gloss. No death.
12:100. He raised abawayhi (his two parents) on the throne. They fell prostrate. This is the taʾwīl of my former vision. Still no Rachel. Still no “she had died.”
3. What tafsīr does with 12:4

Ibn ʿAbbās, Ḍaḥḥāk, Qatāda, Sufyān al-Thawrī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Zayd, and Ibn Kathīr after them: eleven stars = brothers; sun and moon = father and mother. That is Jacob’s Genesis 37:10 gloss, not the midrashic repair. Tanwīr al-Miqbās even names Rachel and Jacob.
4. What tafsīr does with 12:100
Al-Suddī and Ibn Zayd: abawayhi = father and maternal aunt, because the mother had died long ago.
Ibn Isḥāq and al-Ṭabarī: father and mother were both alive. Ṭabarī: there is no evidence that his mother had died before then; the apparent wording of the Quran testifies that she was alive.
Two Muslim answers to one imported problem. Ṭabarī refuses the death. Suddī/Ibn Zayd use the aunt — the Bilhah-class fix under another name.
5. Layer map
Layer 0. Quran: unnamed lights; later two parents. Silent on death.
Layer 1. Standard 12:4 tafsīr: father / mother / brothers (Jacob’s sentence).
Layer 2. Where Genesis chronology is assumed: substitute mother (aunt).
Layer 3. Ṭabarī: the Quran’s wording does not support the death, so do not write it.
Genesis Rabbah is centuries before Islam. Layer 2 resembles its repair. Layer 0 does not state the repair. Layer 3 argues from the Quran against importing the death.
6. IDs
QB-0336. Dead-mother problem: Gen 37:10 + Gen. Rabbah 84:11. Quran 12:4/100 does not name or kill the mother.
QDISC-0641. 12:4 unglossed; 12:100 abawayhi without identifying the second parent or stating a death.
RELATED_BUT_DISTINCT. Midrash, Quran, Suddī, and Ṭabarī remain four records.

packets.title: Comparison Reuben Judah Unnamed Brother
paragraphs: Comparison — Reuben / Judah sequence and the Quran’s unnamed brother
Date: 29 September 2026. DRAFT / UNPUBLISHED. QB-0340. Not a merge.
1. Question

Did pre-Islamic Jewish and Christian Joseph traditions already alter or anonymize the Reuben/Judah sequence? If they did, 12:10 “a speaker among them” and 12:80 “the eldest of them” might reflect a circulating Late Antique telling. If they did not, those Quranic figures are not simply that tradition with the labels peeled off.
2. Genesis sequence (the baseline)

37:21–22 Reuben: do not kill him; put him in the pit, so I may restore him. 37:26–27 Judah: sell him to the Ishmaelites; do not lay a hand on him. 42:37 Reuben offers his two sons as surety. 43:8–9 Judah succeeds in getting Benjamin sent. 44 Judah’s long plea.
3. What Late Antique texts do with those names
Josephus, Antiquities 2. Reuben (Reubel) still speaks first against killing; Judah (Judas) still proposes the sale after Reuben has gone. Speeches are longer. Names stay.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs (Jewish work with Christian transmission; Zebulun / Judah strands). More names, not fewer. Simeon and Gad as would-be killers. Reuben proposes the pit. Judah watches the pit and claims he restrained bloodshed. Zebulun is set to watch. The sequence is expanded and moralized. It is not anonymized.

Syriac History of Joseph (late 4th / early 5th c.). Reuben and Judah both try to protect Joseph. The other brothers suggest the sale against Judah’s wish. Judah still negotiates the price. The roles shift; the names remain.

Early Syriac verse (Ephrem / Narsai line). Simeon: kill. Judah: sell. Reuben: pit. Judah is then typed to Judas Iscariot. The naming is load-bearing for Christian typology. An anonymous speaker would break that type.
Later midrash collections (Ginzberg’s synthesis of earlier haggadah). Reuben still opens; Judah still sells; Simeon throws him in; Zebulun and Judah watch. Again more named actors.
Joseph and Aseneth. Rearranges later brother-plots (Dan, Gad, Simeon, Levi). It does not replace the pit-scene speakers with an unnamed man.
4. What the Quran does
12:10. A speaker among them (qāʾilun minhum): do not kill Joseph; throw him into the bottom of the well; some caravan will pick him up.
12:80. The eldest of them (kabīruhum): I will not leave this land until my father gives leave or God judges for me.

No Reuben. No Judah. No Simeon. The well-speech combines spare-him and caravan in one unnamed mouth. The Egypt-speech is “the eldest,” which can be heard as firstborn without saying Reuben, and it is not Judah’s Genesis 44 plea.
5. Finding

The circulating Late Antique Joseph file, as sampled here, does not anonymize Reuben and Judah. It keeps them and often adds Simeon, Gad, Dan, Zebulun. Some Christian tellings need Judah named in order to type him to Judas.

Therefore 12:10 and 12:80 do not match a well-attested already-anonymous brother. They are a different narrative choice: one unnamed speaker at the well who both spares and routes him to a caravan; later an eldest who stays under the compact.

That can still be a compression of Genesis. It is not evidence that the Quran is simply reprinting a Late Antique Joseph in which those names had already dropped out. Absence of Reuben/Judah from the Recitation is not the same as their absence from the environment.
OPEN: whether some oral Joseph-cycle, not in the texts sampled here, already said “one of them” and “the eldest.” The written Jewish and Christian file we have runs the other way.
6. IDs

QB-0340. Reuben/Judah sequence in Genesis, Josephus, Testaments, Syriac History of Joseph, and Syriac verse, beside 12:10 qāʾilun minhum and 12:80 kabīruhum. RELATED_BUT_DISTINCT. Names stay in the Late Antique file; the Quran does not use them.
QDISC-0657. 12:10 one unnamed speaker both blocks the killing and sends him toward a caravan. 12:80 the eldest stays; not a named Judah plea.

packets.title: S012 Yusuf Probe ALR 12 1 Manuscripts and Explanations
paragraphs: S012 Yūsuf — Probe: الٓر at 12:1
Manuscript witnesses, late-antique scribal parallels, earliest datable Muslim explanations.
Date: 25 September 2026
Namespace: grok. Status: DRAFT / UNPUBLISHED. No Axis D. Does not rewrite WORM v2. Does not merge with ChatGPT records.
Parent unit: S012_Yusuf_CP01_vv001-018_Research.docx (12:1–18). This file is the historical-textual probe requested after that unit, not a replacement of CP01.
1. Question

Trace the earliest manuscript witnesses to Surah 12:1 itself; then pre-Islamic Arabic, Syriac, Aramaic, Hebrew, and Greek scribal parallels; then the earliest datable Muslim explanations. Aim: separate what the copies and the verse show from explanations that appear after an original public meaning — if there was one — may already have been lost.
2. What 12:1 is on the page
الٓر ۚ تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ

Three isolated letters (alif, lām, rāʾ), then: those are the signs of the clear Book. The maddah on lām in printed muṣḥafs is later pointing. Early rasm is three letters in a row, recited as letter-names, not as a lexical word.
Same three letters: 10:1, 11:1, 14:1, 15:1. 13:1 is المر (four letters). الم is a different string. Do not collapse them.
3. Manuscript witnesses to 12:1 itself

The oldest radiocarbon-dated Qurʾān leaves do not contain Yusuf 1. Birmingham Mingana 1572a (parchment 568–645 CE, 95.4%) preserves parts of 18–20. Tübingen (649–675) preserves 17–36. Those dates are real; they are not 12:1.

Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (Ḥijāzī, late 7th / early 8th; BnF Arabe 328ab + St Petersburg Marcel 18 etc.) preserves about 45% of the Qurʾān. Its Yusuf block is 12:84–15:87. It therefore witnesses 15:1 الر, not 12:1. Same letter-string, different verse.

Best early witness located in this pass that includes 12:1 in its surviving run: British Library Or. 2165 (Ḥijāzī II, Fusṭāṭ). Corpus Coranicum range: 7:42–9:95 and 10:9–39:47 and 40:61–43:71. Estimated production before 750. That range covers all of Yusuf, including 12:1. This is palaeographic / catalogue dating, not a published radiocarbon date on the 12:1 folio.

BL Or. 2165
Ḥijāzī II, est. before 750
NLR Marcel 34 (+ BnF Arabe 348d)
Kufic D, est. 700–900
Ṣanʿāʾ DAM 01-13.8
Kufic, est. 750–900

What those early pages show when they have the opening: three rasm letters, then tilka āyātu l-kitābi l-mubīn. Early Ḥijāzī typically has little or no iʿjām and no short-vowel dots. We do not have a companion-period leaf that can be pointed at and said: here is 12:1 in a hand that died before 650.
4. Scribal parallels (function, not parentage)
Pre-Islamic Arabic. Namāra (328 CE) and other Late Antique Arabic inscriptions are continuous words. No pre-Islamic Arabic book-opening of the muqaṭṭaʿāt type has been produced in this pass.

Hebrew. Biblical books do not open with orphan letters. YHWH is a word (the divine name), not a surah-cipher. Later Jewish letter-mysticism (otiyot, gematria) is commentary practice. The modern AL = Hebrew El guess is twentieth-century comparison, not a manuscript reading of 12:1.

Aramaic / Syriac. Letters are used as numbers and sometimes as section marks. Sacred-word abbreviations are recoverable because the community already knows the expanded word. الر is not tagged to a spelled-out expansion on the page.
Greek. Nomina sacra (ΘΣ, ΙΣ, ΧΣ) are contractions of known names, often marked. Recoverable abbreviation. Quranic isolated letters are written as letter-names and are not expanded in the rasm.

What the parallel actually gives: late antique Near Eastern scribes did treat letters as signs (numbers, holy-name shortcuts, decorative initials). That makes الر typologically at home in a world that loads letters with extra work. It does not decode الر. Bellamy’s worn-basmala reconstruction is a modern hypothesis, not an early Muslim report.
5. Earliest datable Muslim explanations
Layer 0 — the Qurʾān. No gloss. After الر it talks about the Book. That is all 12:1 does on the page.

Attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās (d. 68/687–88). Later collections give him both: the letters are names / the greatest name of God, and their meaning is with God. Those reports reach us through later ṣaḥīfas (notably ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭalḥa, d. 120/737), not through an autograph tafsīr. Early circulating opinion, not a dated seventh-century book.

Mujāhid (d. 104/722). Said to have gone through the muṣḥaf with Ibn ʿAbbās verse by verse. The surviving Tafsīr Mujāhid is a later compilation of that stream. Useful as evidence that Successors were already being asked the question. Not a photograph of 12:1’s original briefing.

Muqātil b. Sulaymān (d. 150/767). Earliest extant continuous tafsīr. On 12:1 he explains al-kitāb al-mubīn (makes clear what is in it) and then 12:2–3. He does not, in that opening, give a unique cryptographic key for الر. The letters are already a known class (ḥurūf), not solved.

Al-Ṭabarī (d. 310/923). First large menu: names of God, names of the surah, challenge to the Arabs (your own letters), only God knows, and others. Rāzī later counts about twenty views. That is a tenth-century inventory of a problem that was already old.
No prophetic ḥadīth with a sound, early, specific decoding of الر at 12:1 has been produced in this file. Seven aḥruf is about recitation, not about these three letters.
6. Know / do not know
Know (text + copies):
12:1 is three isolated letters plus “those are the signs of the clear Book.”
The same three letters open 10, 11, 14, 15; 13 adds mīm.
Early Ḥijāzī and Kufic copies write them as letters in the rasm.
By the second Islamic century, Muslims already offer several incompatible explanations.
Do not know:
A first-generation written gloss.
That there ever was a public “original meaning” that could be lost, as opposed to letters meant to remain unglossed.
That Hebrew El, Syriac numerals, or Greek nomina sacra are the source. Possible habits of a scribal world, not demonstrated parents of الر.
Later than the verse (commentary history, not a finding about what 12:1 says): ism Allāh al-aʿẓam readings; abjad keys; half-the-alphabet iʿjāz challenge; Bellamy’s worn basmala; AL = El.
7. IDs (Grok, DRAFT)
ID
Title / statement
QDISC-0618
12:1 الٓر recited as isolated letters, then “those are the signs of the clear Book.” Quran supplies no gloss. Same family as 10:1, 11:1, 14:1, 15:1; not الم or المر.
QDISC-0619
Earliest located copy of 12:1 itself in this pass: BL Or. 2165 (Ḥijāzī, est. pre-750). Older carbon-dated leaves do not contain this verse.
QDISC-0620
CPP witnesses 15:1 الر, not 12:1. Same letter-string, different unit.

QCA-0013 was proposed in chat as a candidate only: explanations of الر as names/numbers/abbreviations are attested from the tafsīr stream, not from the verse; whether an “original meaning” existed and was lost remains OPEN. Not written into the live QCA register in this file. Last live Grok QCA amendment remains QCA-0012 unless separately authorized.
Related earlier IDs (not merged): QDISC-0005 isolated letters at 2:1 ungossed; QDISC-0502 Alif Lam Ra at 10:1. RELATED_BUT_DISTINCT. Preservation Rule applies.
8. Sources used in this pass

Corpus Coranicum catalogue entries for BL Or. 2165, Marcel 34, DAM 01-13.8; Déroche / Wikipedia descriptions of Codex Parisino-petropolitanus and Birmingham; Dutton on Arabe 328a contents (12:84–15:87); Muqātil on 12:1–3; standard notices of Ibn ʿAbbās / ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭalḥa / Ṭabarī on the isolated letters. This is a first-pass inventory, not a folio-by-folio collation of Or. 2165 at 12:1.
9. Next
Optional: page-level rasm check of Or. 2165 at 12:1; dated list of Ṭabarī’s opinions one by one; or resume narrative unit 12:19–35 (QDISC-0621+ if this probe’s IDs are kept).
Parked unchanged: tahrif “they changed the book they possess” through 114; 9:111 three-book promise.

packets.title: S012 Yusuf CP01 vv001-018 Research
paragraphs: S012 Yūsuf — Checkpoint 01
Unit: 12:1–18 (18 verses). Meccan by traditional label.
Date: 25 September 2026

Resume authorization: Architecture v1.0 §73, human OUT_OF_BAND, 2026-09-25. ChatGPT continuation QDISC-1235 / QB-0219 (ChatGPT’s file). This packet is Grok namespace only: QDISC-0609+ / QB-0328+. DRAFT / UNPUBLISHED. No Axis D. No merge.
1. Overview

الر. Those are the signs of the clear Book. We have sent it down as an Arabic Recitation so that you may understand. We relate to you the best of stories in that We have revealed to you this Qurʾān; before it you were among the unaware.

Joseph said to his father: O my father, I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me. He said: O my son, do not recount your vision to your brothers, lest they contrive a plot against you. Satan is to man a clear enemy. Thus your Lord will choose you and teach you interpretation of events and complete His favor on you and on the house of Jacob, as He completed it on your two fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Your Lord is Knowing, Wise.

In Joseph and his brothers were signs for those who ask. They said: Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, though we are a band. Our father is in clear error. Kill Joseph or cast him to a land; your father’s face will be free for you; after that you will be righteous people. A speaker among them said: do not kill Joseph; throw him into the bottom of the well; some caravan will pick him up, if you are going to do something.

They said: O our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph when we are sincere advisers? Send him with us tomorrow to revel and play; we will be his guardians. He said: it grieves me that you should take him, and I fear a wolf may eat him while you are heedless of him. They said: if a wolf eats him while we are a band, we would then be losers.

When they took him and agreed to put him in the bottom of the well, We revealed to him: you will surely inform them of this affair while they do not perceive. They came to their father at night, weeping. They said: we went racing and left Joseph with our things, and the wolf ate him. You will not believe us even if we were truthful. They brought his shirt with false blood. He said: rather your selves have enticed you to a matter. So patience is beautiful. God is the one whose help is sought against what you describe.
2. Structure

1–3 frame: isolated letters; clear Book; Arabic Recitation for understanding; best of stories; addressee previously unaware. 4–6 vision and paternal warning; election, taʾwīl, completed favor on Jacob’s house as on Abraham and Isaac. 7 signs for those who ask. 8–10 plot: love-jealousy; kill or exile; one speaker substitutes the well so a caravan takes him. 11–14 petition and wolf-fear. 15 well + revelation to Joseph while they do not perceive. 16–18 night return, wolf-lie, false blood on the shirt, ṣabr jamīl.
3. Investigation

The unit is a framed narrative, not a free novella. 12:3 calls the following aḥsan al-qaṣaṣ and ties it to “this Recitation,” so the story is presented as revealed teaching, not recovered folklore. 12:2 makes Arabic the vehicle of understanding; that is a language claim about this Recitation, not a claim that earlier Joseph-material was Arabic.

The vision (11 stars, sun, moon, sujūd) is told once and immediately sealed by the father: do not tell your brothers. The plot is jealousy of paternal love, with “his brother” (Benjamin, unnamed here) grouped with Joseph. The well-plan is attributed to “a speaker among them,” not named. Killing is proposed and then displaced. At the bottom of the well God addresses Joseph with a future-telling: he will report this affair to them while they do not perceive. That wahy is not given to the father or the brothers in this unit.

The wolf is the father’s fear first (12:13), then the brothers’ cover story (12:17). The shirt with false blood is their exhibit. The father’s reply does not ratify the wolf; he names nafs-enticement and asks beautiful patience. No Egyptian scene yet. No named wife, no prison, no famine. Do not import Genesis details that this unit does not state.
4. Lemmas

الْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ — the Book described as making-clear / clear. قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا — an Arabic Recitation (12:2). أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ — the best of stories / narration (12:3). غَافِلِينَ — unaware (12:3). كَوْكَبًا / الشَّمْسَ / الْقَمَرَ / سَاجِدِينَ — stars, sun, moon, prostrating (12:4). كَيْدًا — a plot (12:5). تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ — interpretation of events/narratives (12:6). آيَاتٌ لِلسَّائِلِينَ — signs for those who ask (12:7). عُصْبَةٌ — a band/clan (12:8, 14). غَيَابَتِ الْجُبِّ — the bottom/hidden part of the well (12:10, 15). الذِّئْبُ — the wolf (12:13, 17). أَوْحَيْنَا — We revealed (12:15). دَمٍ كَذِبٍ — false/lying blood (12:18). فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ — beautiful patience (12:18).
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Loci that split: 12:2 qurʾānan ʿarabiyyan; 12:3 aḥsan al-qaṣaṣ and min al-ghāfilīn; 12:6 taʾwīl al-aḥādīth; 12:10 / 15 ghayābat al-jubb; 12:18 ṣabr jamīl and dam kidhb.

Arabic remains primary. Sahih International, Abdel Haleem, Pickthall, and Arberry agree that 12:2 is an Arabic Qurʾān/Recitation sent down so the addressee’s people may understand. They do not turn 12:2 into a claim about the language of Genesis. aḥsan al-qaṣaṣ is “best of stories” (SI, Pickthall) or “best of narratives.” Haleem’s “fairest of stories” is tone, not a different proposition. taʾwīl al-aḥādīth is “interpretation of events/narratives/dreams.” The Arabic is aḥādīth, not exclusively “dreams”; dream-reading is the later plot function, not the only sense of the lemma here. ghayābat al-jubb is the concealed depth of a well/cistern, not a named pit in Canaan. ṣabr jamīl is “beautiful/fitting patience,” not mere endurance. dam kidhb is blood that is a lie — the shirt is evidence fabricated, not evidence assessed as true.
Yusuf Ali 12:18 line only: 'Patience is most fitting: Against that which ye assert, it is Allah (alone) Whose help can be sought.'
6. Theological Findings

The Recitation frames Joseph as revealed “best of stories,” in Arabic, for understanding. Election and taʾwīl are promised before the betrayal. Satan is named as enemy in the father’s warning, not as the brothers’ inner speaker. God speaks to Joseph in the well before any human rescue. The father’s first theological act in the lie-scene is ṣabr jamīl and istiʿāna, not ratification of the wolf. Favor-language in 12:6 ties Joseph to Abraham and Isaac by completed niʿma on Jacob’s house — a continuity claim, not a genealogy lesson.
7–9. Cross / QB

Internal: 12:4–5 vision sealed; fulfillment is later in 12:100 (not in this unit — do not close it here). 12:2 Arabic Recitation sits with 12:3 “this Qurʾān.” 41:3 / 43:3 Arabic Recitation cluster remains parked as language-of-revelation, not as tahrif. Biblical: Genesis 37 is the nearest narrative neighbor — coat, jealousy, pit, sale talk, bloodied garment, father mourns. Differences that this unit already shows: eleven stars + sun + moon (Genesis 37:9 has sun, moon, eleven stars); Quran names the wolf as the father’s fear and the brothers’ lie; Genesis 37 has no “We revealed to him in the well you will tell them of this affair”; Genesis names Reuben and Judah in the spare-him debate; Quran says “a speaker among them.” Shirt in Quran carries false blood; Genesis 37:31–33 a slaughtered goat on the coat. Do not merge the two tellings.
ID
Title
QDISC-0609
Clear Book; Arabic Recitation sent down so you may understand (12:1–2)
QDISC-0610
Best of stories in this Qurʾān; addressee was among the unaware (12:3)
QDISC-0611
Eleven stars, sun, and moon seen prostrating; father bars retelling (12:4–5)
QDISC-0612
Election, taʾwīl of events, completed favor on Jacob’s house as on Abraham and Isaac (12:6)
QDISC-0613
Signs in Joseph and his brothers for those who ask (12:7)
QDISC-0614
Jealousy plot: kill or cast out; a speaker substitutes the well for a caravan (12:8–10)
QDISC-0615
Trust-petition, play, wolf-fear, band-boast (12:11–14)
QDISC-0616
Well-agreement; revelation to Joseph that he will later tell them, while they do not perceive (12:15)
QDISC-0617
Night weeping; wolf-lie; shirt with false blood; ṣabr jamīl and help sought from God (12:16–18)
Joseph’s vision — sun, moon, eleven stars (Genesis 37:9 neighbor; Quran 12:4)
Brothers’ plot, pit/well, bloodied garment (Genesis 37:18–33 neighbor; Quran 12:8–18)
Unnamed “speaker among them” vs named Reuben/Judah spare-him speeches
21–22. Next
12:19–35 — caravan, sale, Egyptian house, attempted seduction, prison-door. Do not write that unit in this file.
Parked (unchanged): tahrif “they changed the book they possess” test through 114; 9:111 three-book promise; 7:157 cluster already filed.
ChatGPT is not written here. Their next IDs if they walk this unit: QDISC-1235+ / QB-0219+.

packets.title: Comparison Quran 12 4 Genesis 37 9
paragraphs: Comparison — Quran 12:4 and Genesis 37:9–11
Date: 29 September 2026. Grok QB-0328 restated. DRAFT / UNPUBLISHED. Not a merge.
1. The two texts
Quran 12:4. إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ
Joseph said to his father: O my father, I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.
Immediate sequel, 12:5, is part of the comparison because it is the father’s answer in the same breath: do not recount your vision to your brothers, lest they contrive a plot. Satan is a clear enemy.

Genesis 37:9–11. He dreamed another dream and told it to his brothers: the sun, the moon, and eleven stars were bowing down to me. He told his father and his brothers. His father rebuked him: Shall we indeed come, I and your mother and your brothers, to bow to the ground before you? His brothers were jealous. His father kept the saying.
2. Shared
Eleven stars. Sun. Moon. They bow or prostrate to Joseph. The vision is told inside the family. The father reacts. Jealousy of the brothers is the next danger in both tellings.
3. Not the same
Audience. Quran: Joseph speaks to his father. The brothers are not in the scene. Genesis: he tells the brothers first, then father and brothers together.
Number of dreams. Genesis 37:5–8 is a first dream, sheaves bowing. 37:9 is another dream. Quran 12:4 is one vision. No sheaf-dream in Yusuf.

Father’s act. Quran 12:5: do not tell your brothers; they will plot; Satan is an enemy. Genesis 37:10: rebuke, and an interpretation — I, your mother, and your brothers will bow. Genesis 37:11: the father keeps the saying.
Gloss. Quran 12:4 does not say who the stars, sun, and moon are. That reading is not given until 12:100, which is outside this verse. Genesis puts the family-gloss in the father’s mouth at once.
Verb. Quran: sājidīn, prostrating. Genesis: bowing to the ground. Neighbor verbs, not one lemma.
4. What not to do
Do not write the sheaf-dream into 12:4. Do not write the mother’s bow into 12:4. Do not close the vision with 12:100 in this comparison. Do not treat Genesis 37:10 as the Quran’s interpretation.
5. ID
QB-0328. Joseph’s vision — sun, moon, eleven stars. Quran 12:4 beside Genesis 37:9. RELATED_BUT_DISTINCT. Preservation Rule: both texts stay.

packets.title: S012 Yusuf CP02 vv019-035 Research
paragraphs: S012 Yūsuf — Checkpoint 02
Unit: 12:19–35 (17 verses). Meccan by traditional label.
Date: 25 September 2026
Grok namespace only. DRAFT / UNPUBLISHED. No Axis D. No merge. WORM v2 not rewritten. ChatGPT continuation remains QDISC-1235 / QB-0219 on their file.
1. Overview

A caravan came. They sent their water-drawer. He let down his bucket. He said: good news — this is a boy. They hid him as merchandise. God was Knowing of what they did. They sold him for a low price, counted dirhams; they were of those who were indifferent about him.

The one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife: honor his lodging. It may be that he will benefit us or we may take him as a son. Thus We established Joseph in the land, and that We might teach him interpretation of events. God is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know. When he reached his full strength, We gave him judgment and knowledge. Thus We repay those who do good.

She in whose house he was sought to make him yield to herself. She shut the doors and said: come here. He said: I take refuge with God. He is my lord who made my stay good. The wrongdoers do not prosper. She desired him, and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Thus, that We might turn evil and indecency from him. He was one of Our chosen servants.

They raced to the door. She tore his shirt from behind. They found her master at the door. She said: what is the recompense of one who intended evil toward your family except prison or a painful punishment? He said: she sought to make me yield. A witness from her family witnessed: if his shirt is torn from the front, she has told the truth and he is of the liars; if torn from behind, she has lied and he is of the truthful. When he saw his shirt torn from behind he said: this is of your (women’s) plot. Your plot is great. Joseph, turn away from this. You (woman), ask forgiveness for your sin. You have been of the sinners.

Women in the city said: the wife of the ʿazīz is seeking her young man. He has smitten her with love. We see her in clear error. When she heard their scheming she sent for them, prepared a reclining, and gave each a knife. She said: come out to them. When they saw him they extolled him and cut their hands. They said: God save us. This is no human. This is no other than a noble angel. She said: this is the one you blamed me for. I did seek to make him yield, and he abstained. If he does not do what I command him, he will be imprisoned and be of the humbled. He said: my Lord, prison is more beloved to me than what they call me to. Unless You turn their plot from me I will incline toward them and be of the ignorant. His Lord answered him and turned their plot from him. He is the Hearing, the Knowing. Then it appeared to them, after they had seen the signs, that they should imprison him for a time.
2. Structure

19–20 recovery and sale: bucket, “boy,” hidden as merchandise, low counted price, indifference. 21–22 establishment in Egypt: honor his lodging; possible adoption; We established him; taʾwīl promised again; ḥukm and ʿilm at maturity. 23–24 closed doors; hayta lak; maʿādh Allāh; double desire checked by the Lord’s proof; evil and faḥisha turned away; mukhlaṣīn. 25–29 race, shirt from behind, master at the door, her accusation, his denial, family-witness rule (front/back), kayd declared great, ṣafḥ + her istighfār. 30–32 city women, banquet, knives, cut hands, angel-speech, she admits the attempt and threatens prison. 33–35 Joseph chooses prison over their call; Lord turns the plot; they still imprison him after seeing the signs.
3. Investigation

The well of 12:15 is left without a named rescuer. 12:19 is a caravan and a water-drawer who finds a boy. They conceal him as merchandise. God knows. The sale in 12:20 is cheap and counted; the sellers are “indifferent about him.” The Quran does not name the price in shekels, does not name Midianites or Ishmaelites, and does not name the buyer.

The buyer is “the one who bought him from Egypt.” He speaks to his wife: honor the lodging; perhaps benefit or a son. The establishment formula (makkannā) and taʾwīl of events recall 12:6. Maturity brings ḥukm and ʿilm as repayment of those who do good — not yet dream-office.

The seduction scene names neither woman nor husband at first: “she in whose house he was.” Doors are shut. His first word is refuge with God; “he is my rabb who made my stay good” can be read as God or as the household master — the Arabic rabb is the same lemma. Do not flatten that. 12:24 is the sharp verse: she desired him; he would have desired her had he not seen his Lord’s proof. The Quran does not describe the proof. It states the purpose: turn away sūʾ and faḥisha. He is among the mukhlaṣīn / mukhliṣīn (both readings exist later; the rasm is shared).

The shirt is torn from behind while they race to the door. The master is there. She speaks first and frames prison or painful punishment. Joseph answers with one clause: she sought to make me yield. The witness is “from her family,” unnamed, and offers a physical test: front of shirt vs back. The back-tear decides. The husband (still not called ʿazīz until 12:30, in the women’s gossip) names kayd as great and splits the verdict: Joseph turn away; she seek forgiveness.

The city women introduce the title ʿazīz and the word fatā (her young man / servant). The banquet with knives is her public counter-plot. They cut their hands and deny he is bashar. She then admits the attempt and threatens prison if he will not do what she commands. Joseph’s prayer prefers prison to “what they call me to.” The Lord turns their plot. 12:35 is the remaining sting: after the signs, they still decide to imprison him for a time. Vindication in the house does not prevent the jail.

Do not write Potiphar, Zuleikha, or a named captain of the guard into this unit. Those names are Genesis / later Islamic storytelling. The Quran in 19–35 has a water-drawer, a buyer from Egypt, his wife, a family witness, city women, and the ʿazīz as a title in gossip.
4. Lemmas

سَيَّارَة — caravan. وَارِدَهُمْ — their water-drawer. بُشْرَىٰ هَٰذَا غُلَامٌ — good news, a boy. بِضَاعَة — merchandise. بَخْسٍ دَرَاهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ — low / deficient counted dirhams. الزَّاهِدِينَ — those indifferent. أَكْرِمِي مَثْوَاهُ — honor his lodging. نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَدًا — take him as a son. مَكَّنَّا — We established. حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا — judgment and knowledge. رَاوَدَتْهُ — she sought to make him yield. هَيْتَ لَكَ — come here. مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ — I take refuge with God. بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ — proof of his Lord. الْفَحْشَاء — indecency. الْمُخْلَصِينَ — chosen / made-sincere. قَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِن دُبُرٍ — tore his shirt from behind. شَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا — a witness from her family. كَيْدُكُنَّ — your (f. pl.) plot. الْعَزِيزِ — the ʿazīz. فَتَاهَا — her young man. أَكْبَرْنَهُ — they extolled him. حَاشَ لِلَّهِ — God save us. مَا هَٰذَا بَشَرًا — this is not a human. مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ — a noble angel. السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ — prison is more beloved to me. فَصَرَفَ — He turned away (the plot).
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Split loci: 12:20 bakhs / dirhams; 12:23 rabbī; 12:24 “he would have desired her” + burhān; 12:26–28 shirt test; 12:31 bashar / malak; 12:33 prison dearer.

Arabic primary. SI, Haleem, Pickthall, Arberry all keep the sale cheap and counted. They all keep the counterfactual desire in 12:24; none erase Joseph’s capacity to desire. rabbī in 12:23 is “my lord” — God or the husband; translations split by capitalization, not by a second Arabic word. hayta laka is an imperative of approach; “come here / come on.” Witness-from-her-family is left unnamed in all five. Yusuf Ali 12:33 line only: “O my Lord! the prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me.”
6. Theological Findings

God knows the concealment (19) and establishes Joseph in the land before the trial in the house (21). Taʾwīl promised in 12:6 is restated as purpose of the establishment. 12:24 refuses both a sexless Joseph and an unchecked fall: desire is admitted as possible; the Lord’s proof interrupts it; the stated aim is to turn away evil and faḥisha. The shirt-from-behind is public evidence inside the house. Kayd is named as the women’s plot and called great — after the evidence, not instead of it. Prison is Joseph’s chosen lesser evil, then the court’s decision after signs. Vindication and imprisonment stand in the same unit.
7–9. Cross / QB

Internal: 12:6 election/taʾwīl → 12:21 establishment/taʾwīl. 12:15 wahy in the well is not repeated here; rescue is a caravan. 12:35 prison “for a time” opens the next unit (cups, dreams) — do not write 12:36–42 in this file. Biblical neighbor Genesis 37:28 (sale) and 39 (house, wife, garment, prison). Differences already visible: Quran unnamed buyer and wife; family witness and front/back shirt test; city women and knives; Joseph’s prayer choosing prison; “they imprisoned him after seeing the signs.” Genesis 39:12 garment left in her hand as he fled; no banquet of women in Genesis 39. Do not merge.

packets.title: S012 Yusuf CP03 vv036-053 Research
paragraphs: S012 Yūsuf — Checkpoint 03
Unit: 12:36–53 (18 verses). Meccan by traditional label.
Date: 29 September 2026
Grok namespace only. DRAFT / UNPUBLISHED. No Axis D. No merge. WORM v2 not rewritten. ChatGPT continuation remains QDISC-1235 / QB-0219 on their file.
1. Overview

Two young men entered the prison with him. One said: I saw myself pressing wine. The other: I saw myself carrying bread on my head, and birds eating from it. Tell us its taʾwīl. We see you among those who do good.

He said: no food will come to you as provision but I will tell you its taʾwīl before it comes to you. That is of what my Lord taught me. I have left the millah of a people who do not believe in God and who deny the hereafter. I followed the millah of my fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with God. That is of God’s favor on us and on the people, but most people do not give thanks.

O my two prison-companions: are scattered lords better, or God the One, the Dominant? You worship, besides Him, only names you and your fathers named, for which God sent down no authority. Judgment belongs only to God. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the straight religion, but most people do not know.

O my two prison-companions: as for one of you, he will pour wine for his lord. As for the other, he will be crucified and birds will eat from his head. The matter you asked about is decided. He said to the one he thought would be saved: mention me to your lord. Satan made him forget the mention to his lord, so he stayed in prison several years.

The king said: I see seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears and others dry. O chiefs, give me a fatwā on my vision if you interpret visions. They said: confused dreams, and we are not of the knowing in the interpretation of dreams. The one of the two who was saved remembered after a time and said: I will tell you its taʾwīl; send me.

Joseph, O truthful one, give us a fatwā on seven fat cows eaten by seven lean, and seven green ears and others dry, that I may return to the people and that they may know. He said: you will sow seven years as usual. What you harvest, leave in its ear, except a little you eat. Then after that come seven hard years that consume what you stored for them, except a little you keep back. Then after that comes a year in which people are given rain and in which they press.

The king said: bring him to me. When the messenger came to him he said: return to your lord and ask him what was the case of the women who cut their hands. My Lord is Knowing of their plot. He said: what was your affair when you sought to make Joseph yield? They said: God save us; we know no evil against him. The wife of the ʿazīz said: now the truth has come out. I sought to make him yield, and he is of the truthful.

That, so he may know I did not betray him in absence, and that God does not guide the plot of the treacherous. I do not acquit myself. The self commands evil except as my Lord has mercy. My Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.
2. Structure

36 two prison dreams. 37–40 teaching before the answer: provision-taʾwīl from the Lord; millah of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob; no shirk; names without authority; judgment is God’s. 41 the two outcomes. 42 mention me — Satan makes him forget — several years. 43–44 king’s seven-and-seven; chiefs call it confused dreams. 45–49 the saved one returns; Joseph’s seven sow / seven hard / one year of rain and pressing. 50–51 summons refused until the women are asked; they clear him; the ʿazīz’s wife confesses. 52–53 “I did not betray him in absence” / “I do not acquit myself” — speaker not named in the Arabic.
3. Investigation

The two men are fatan, young men, not named. One presses wine, one carries bread for birds to eat from his head. Joseph does not answer the dreams first. He claims that food-taʾwīl comes from what his Lord taught him, then states a millah: he left a people who deny God and the hereafter, and followed Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Association is not for them. The prison speech is monotheism before interpretation.
12:40 is a claim about the gods they serve: names named by them and their fathers, no authority sent down. Judgment is only God’s. That is the straight dīn. Most people do not know.

12:41 decides both cases. One pours wine for his lord. The other is crucified and birds eat from his head. The matter is decided. 12:42 is the failure of the human plan: Joseph asks the one he thinks will be saved to mention him to his lord. Satan makes him forget the mention. Joseph stays years. The text does not say Joseph sinned by asking; it says the mention was forgotten by Satan’s making.

The king’s vision is one report: seven fat cows eaten by seven lean, and seven green ears and others dry. The chiefs refuse interpretation: aḍghāth aḥlām. The saved companion remembers after a span and asks to be sent. Joseph is still addressed in prison as the truthful one. His reading is agricultural: seven years of sowing, grain left in the ear, seven hard years that consume the store, then a year of rain and pressing. He is not yet released.

12:50 is the hinge. The king says bring him. The messenger arrives. Joseph sends him back: ask your lord about the women who cut their hands. Release is refused until the old charge is reopened. 12:51 is the inquiry. The women: we know no sūʾ against him. The wife of the ʿazīz: the truth has come out; I sought him; he is of the truthful.

12:52–53 do not name the speaker. “So he may know I did not betray him in absence” can be read as the woman’s speech about her husband, or as Joseph’s speech about the ʿazīz. “I do not acquit myself; the self commands evil except as my Lord has mercy” is the next sentence. Do not assign the speaker in the QDISC line. Record the ambiguity.
Do not write Pharaoh, butler, or baker into the finding titles. The Quran has a king, a lord of the cup-pourer, two young men, and the wife of the ʿazīz.
4. Lemmas

فَتَيَانِ — two young men. أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا — I press wine. خُبْزًا … تَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ — bread, birds eat. تَأْوِيلِهِ — its interpretation. مِلَّةَ — millah. آبَائِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ — my fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. أَرْبَابٌ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ — scattered lords. اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ — God the One, the Dominant. أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا — names you named. سُلْطَانٍ — authority. الْحُكْمُ — judgment. الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ — the straight religion. يَسْقِي رَبَّهُ خَمْرًا — pours wine for his lord. يُصْلَبُ — he will be crucified. أَذْكُرْنِي عِندَ رَبِّكَ — mention me to your lord. فَأَنسَاهُ الشَّيْطَانُ — Satan made him forget. بِضْعَ سِنِينَ — several years. الْمَلِكُ — the king. سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ — seven fat cows. أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ — confused dreams. أَيُّهَا الصِّدِّيقُ — O truthful one. دَأَبًا — as usual / diligently. سَنَابِلَ — ears. يُغَاثُ النَّاسُ — people are given rain. يَعْصِرُونَ — they press. قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ — they cut their hands. حَاشَ لِلَّهِ — God save us. بِالْغَيْبِ — in absence. النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ — the self commands evil.
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Split loci: 12:36 “press wine”; 12:39–40 scattered lords / names without authority; 12:42 “his lord” and who forgot; 12:44 aḍghāth aḥlām; 12:49 yughāthu / yaʿṣirūn; 12:52–53 speaker.

Arabic primary. SI, Haleem, Pickthall, and Arberry keep both prison outcomes and the seven-year agricultural reading. They differ on whether 12:42’s “lord” is the king and on who speaks 12:52–53. That second split is not solved by the Arabic pronouns alone. Yusuf Ali 12:42 line only: “Mention me to thy lord.”
6. Theological Findings

Taʾwīl in prison is claimed as teaching from the Lord, then tied to the millah of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to a refusal of association. Judgment is only God’s. Human rescue fails: the mention is forgotten for years. The king’s dream is read as provision-policy, not as Joseph’s office yet. Release is refused until the women clear him. The wife’s confession and the unnamed self-accusation stand in the same close. Do not collapse 12:52–53 into one speaker.
7–9. Cross / QB

Internal: 12:6 and 12:21 taʾwīl restated in 12:37 as what the Lord taught. 12:31 cut hands reopened in 12:50. 12:35 prison “for a time” becomes “several years” in 12:42. Abraham–Isaac–Jacob millah links to 12:6 completed favor. Biblical neighbor: Genesis 40 cupbearer and baker; Genesis 41 Pharaoh’s two dreams of seven cows and seven ears. Differences already visible: Quran one king-vision containing cows and ears; chiefs call it confused dreams; Joseph will not come out until the women are questioned; Genesis 41 brings him out at once after the interpretation. Do not merge.

QDISC-0632

QDISC-0633

packets.title: S012 Yusuf CP04 vv054-068 Research
paragraphs: S012 Yūsuf — Checkpoint 04
Unit: 12:54–68 (15 verses). Meccan by traditional label.
Date: 29 September 2026. Grok namespace. DRAFT / UNPUBLISHED. No Axis D. No merge. ChatGPT still QDISC-1235 / QB-0219 on their file.
Prior: CP01–03 through 12:53; ALR probe; dead-mother comparison QB-0336 / QDISC-0641.
1. Overview

The king said: bring him to me. I will attach him to myself. When he spoke to him he said: you are today with us established, trusted. Joseph said: appoint me over the storehouses of the land. I am a knowing guardian. Thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle in it where he willed. We strike with Our mercy whom We will. We do not waste the wage of those who do good. The wage of the hereafter is better for those who believe and are wary.

The brothers of Joseph came and entered upon him. He recognized them; they did not recognize him. When he had furnished them with their provisions he said: bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts? If you do not bring him, there is no measure for you with me, and do not come near me. They said: we will seek to lure him from his father. We will do it.

He said to his pages: put their merchandise in their packs. Perhaps they will recognize it when they turn back to their family; perhaps they will return. When they returned to their father they said: measure has been denied us. Send our brother with us that we may obtain measure. We will be his guardians. He said: shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother before? God is the best guardian, the most merciful of the merciful.

When they opened their things they found their merchandise returned to them. They said: O our father, what more do we seek? This is our merchandise returned to us. We will provision our family, guard our brother, and increase a camel’s measure. That is an easy measure. He said: I will not send him with you until you give me a compact from God that you will bring him to me unless you are surrounded. When they gave him their compact he said: God is trustee over what we say.

He said: O my sons, do not enter by one gate; enter by different gates. I avail you nothing against God. Judgment is only God’s. On Him I rely; on Him let the reliant rely. When they entered as their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against God at all — only a need in Jacob’s soul that he satisfied. He was a possessor of knowledge because We had taught him, but most people do not know.
2. Structure

54–57 office: king attaches him; Joseph asks for the storehouses; We established him; mercy and wage; hereafter better. 58–61 first recognition: he knows them, they do not; demand the other brother; they will lure him. 62 merchandise put back as a return-hook. 63–66 at home: measure denied; Jacob’s distrust of the earlier trust; returned goods; compact from God unless surrounded. 67–68 different gates; judgment only God’s; the order does not avail against God; a need in Jacob’s soul; knowledge taught.
3. Investigation

The king’s line is attachment and trust (makīn amīn). Joseph does not wait to be assigned. He asks for the storehouses and names himself ḥafīẓ ʿalīm. 12:56 repeats the establishment formula of 12:21, now as settlement where he wills. 12:57 pulls the wage off this world.

The brothers enter. Recognition is one-way. He does not reveal himself. The demand is “a brother of yours from your father” — Benjamin is not named. Full measure and hospitality are the bait; no measure and no approach are the threat. They say they will seek to lure him from the father.

The returned merchandise is Joseph’s device, not a miracle-claim in the verse. Purpose stated: perhaps they will recognize it and return. At home Jacob’s first answer is the old wound: shall I trust you as I trusted you with his brother before? Then the packs are opened and the goods argue for a second trip. Jacob will not send him without a compact from God, with one exception: unless you are surrounded.

12:67–68 is the theological close of the unit. Different gates. I cannot avail you against God. Judgment is only God’s — the same ḥukm lemma as 12:40. The entry as ordered does not avail against God. What remains is a need in Jacob’s soul that he satisfied. He has knowledge because We taught him. Most people do not know.
Do not write Pharaoh, Potiphar, or Simeon-as-hostage into the titles. The Quran has a king, storehouses, unnamed brothers, an unnamed other brother, and Jacob.
4. Lemmas

أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ — I will attach him to myself. مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ — established, trusted. خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ — storehouses of the land. حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ — knowing guardian. مَكَّنَّا — We established. عَرَفَهُمْ — he recognized them. هُم لَهُ مُنكِرُونَ — they did not recognize him. أَخًا لَّكُم مِّنْ أَبِيكُمْ — a brother of yours from your father. الْكَيْلَ — the measure. نُرَاوِدُ — we will seek to lure. بِضَاعَتَهُمْ — their merchandise. اللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَافِظًا — God is the best guardian. مَوْثِقًا مِّنَ اللَّهِ — a compact from God. إِلَّا أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ — unless you are surrounded. بَابٍ وَاحِدٍ / أَبْوَابٍ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٍ — one gate / different gates. الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ — judgment only God’s. حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ — a need in Jacob’s soul.
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Split loci: 12:54 astakhliṣuhu; 12:55 ḥafīẓ ʿalīm; 12:61 nurāwidu; 12:66 yuḥāṭa bikum; 12:68 ḥājah in Jacob’s soul.

Arabic primary. SI, Haleem, Pickthall, Arberry keep one-way recognition and the returned packs. “Surrounded” / “prevented” / “overwhelmed” is the 12:66 split. Yusuf Ali 12:55 line only: “Set me over the store-houses of the land: I will indeed guard them, as one that knows.”
6. Theological Findings

Office is asked for, then named as God’s establishment and mercy. Recognition is withheld. Jacob’s trust-language returns the first betrayal. The compact is from God, with one exception clause. Different gates do not bind God. Ḥukm is only His — restated from the prison speech. Jacob’s knowledge is taught, not inferred from the gate-plan’s success.
7–9. Cross / QB
Internal: 12:21 makkannā → 12:56. 12:40 ḥukm only God’s → 12:67. 12:64 trust as before = 12:13–18 wound still open. Next unit is the cup, not this file.

Biblical neighbor: Genesis 41:39–49 office; Genesis 42 first visit, money in the sacks, demand for Benjamin. Differences: Quran Joseph requests the storehouses; king attaches him as makīn amīn; no named hostage left in Egypt in this unit; Jacob orders different gates and the text says it did not avail against God. Do not merge.

packets.title: S012 Yusuf CP05 vv069-082 Research
paragraphs: S012 Yūsuf — Checkpoint 05
Unit: 12:69–82 (14 verses). Meccan by traditional label.
Date: 29 September 2026. Grok namespace. DRAFT / UNPUBLISHED. No Axis D. No merge.
Prior: CP04 12:54–68 (QDISC-0642–0649). Compact of 12:66 still open.
1. Overview

When they entered upon Joseph he took his brother to himself. He said: I am your brother, so do not despair of what they used to do. When he had furnished them with their provisions he put the drinking-cup in his brother’s pack. Then a crier cried: O caravan, you are thieves.

They said, turning to them: what is it you miss? They said: we miss the king’s ṣuwāʿ. Whoever brings it shall have a camel-load, and I am its guarantor. They said: by God, you know we did not come to work corruption in the land, and we were not thieves. They said: what is its recompense if you are liars? They said: its recompense is that he in whose pack it is found — he is its recompense. Thus we repay the wrongdoers.

He began with their bags before his brother’s bag, then he brought it out from his brother’s bag. Thus We plotted for Joseph. He was not to take his brother under the king’s dīn except that God willed. We raise in degrees whom We will. Over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows.

They said: if he steals, a brother of his has stolen before. Joseph hid it in himself and did not show it to them. He said: you are in a worse place, and God knows best what you describe. They said: O ʿazīz, he has a father, an aged great one. Take one of us in his place. We see you among those who do good. He said: God forbid that we should take anyone except him with whom we found our property. Then we would be wrongdoers.

When they despaired of him they withdrew privately. The eldest of them said: do you not know that your father has taken from you a compact from God, and before that you failed concerning Joseph? I will not leave this land until my father gives me leave or God judges for me. He is the best of judges. Return to your father and say: O our father, your son has stolen. We testify only to what we know. We were not guardians of the unseen. Ask the town we were in and the caravan we came with. We are truthful.
2. Structure

69 private recognition of the brother. 70 cup planted; crier: thieves. 71–75 missing object named as the king’s ṣuwāʿ; camel-load reward; they deny theft; they themselves set the penalty: the one in whose pack it is found. 76 search order; cup from the brother’s pack; We plotted for Joseph; not under the king’s dīn except God willed. 77 they smear a brother who stole before; Joseph hides his answer. 78–79 they offer a substitute; he refuses anyone but the one with the property. 80–82 private council; eldest will not leave; message for the father: your son stole; we testify to what we know; ask the town and the caravan.
3. Investigation

12:69 is the first time Joseph speaks his identity to anyone from the family: I am your brother. It is to this one brother only. The others still do not know him. The cup is then put in that brother’s pack. The public cry is theft. The object is the king’s ṣuwāʿ, not named as Joseph’s private cup in this verse.

The brothers propose the penalty themselves: the one in whose pack it is found, he is its recompense. That matches a person-for-property taking. 12:76 says We plotted (kidnā) for Joseph. He could not take his brother under the king’s dīn except that God willed. The Quran contrasts two legal frames and says God made the taking possible. It does not name Egyptian statute.

12:77 is their smear: if he steals, a brother of his stole before. Joseph does not answer them in public. He hides it in himself. 12:78 they appeal to the aged father and offer a substitute body. He refuses anyone but the one with whom the property was found.

12:80 the eldest (kabīruhum) will not leave the land until the father permits or God judges. That is the compact of 12:66 coming due. The message they send is “your son has stolen,” plus a limit: we testify only to what we know; we were not guardians of the unseen; ask the town and the caravan.
Do not write Benjamin, Judah, or Simeon into the ID titles. The Quran has “his brother,” “the eldest of them,” and the ʿazīz as the title they use for Joseph.
4. Lemmas

آوَى إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ — he took his brother to himself. السِّقَايَةَ — the drinking-cup. الْعِيرُ — the caravan. لَسَارِقُونَ — you are thieves. صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ — the king’s cup. حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ — a camel-load. جَزَاؤُهُ — its recompense. كِدْنَا لِيُوسُفَ — We plotted for Joseph. دِينِ الْمَلِكِ — the king’s dīn. فَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ — over every knower is One who knows. سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ — a brother of his stole before. أَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِي نَفْسِهِ — Joseph hid it in himself. شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا — an aged great one. كَبِيرُهُمْ — the eldest of them. مَوْثِقًا — compact. نَشْهَدُ إِلَّا بِمَا عَلِمْنَا — we testify only to what we know. الْغَيْبِ — the unseen.
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Split loci: 12:70 siqāyah vs 12:72 ṣuwāʿ; 12:76 kidnā / dīn al-malik; 12:77 “a brother stole before”; 12:80 kabīruhum.

Arabic primary. The five keep the cup-plant and the self-proposed penalty. dīn al-malik is law / religion / custom of the king — do not flatten. Yusuf Ali 12:76 line only: “Thus did We plan for Joseph.”
6. Theological Findings

Private recognition first. Public plot second. God is named as the plotter for Joseph, with a limit: not under the king’s dīn except by God’s will. Knowledge has a ceiling: over every knower is One who knows. The smear about an earlier theft is left unanswered in public. The eldest binds himself to the compact and to God’s judgment. Their testimony is capped: only what we know; we were not guardians of the unseen.
7–9. Cross / QB

Internal: 12:66 compact → 12:80. 12:23 rāwadat and 12:61 nurāwidu are not reused here; this unit is kayd attributed to God. 12:77 “a brother stole before” is their claim, not a QDISC that Joseph stole. Next: Jacob’s grief and the shirt of 12:83–98, not this file.

Biblical neighbor: Genesis 44 cup in Benjamin’s sack; Judah’s speech. Differences: Quran private “I am your brother” before the plant; God plotted; king’s dīn clause; eldest stays rather than Judah’s long plea in this unit; “a brother stole before” has no Genesis 44 parallel. Do not merge.
